Definition: Abbreviated author initials and surnames separated by semicolons (e.g., “R., Williams, Rob; K.D., Cox, Kieran D.”).
Full names of all authors with unique Scopus Author IDs in parentheses, separated by semicolons.
List of Scopus Author IDs corresponding to each author, separated by semicolons.
Full title of the publication.
Year the publication was released.
Number of citations the article has received (from Scopus).
Digital Object Identifier (DOI) for the article.
Direct Scopus URL to the publication record.
Institutional affiliations and countries of all authors, separated by semicolons.
Combined field listing each author followed by their institutional affiliation and country.
Abstract text of the article summarizing the main findings.
Author-supplied keywords (semicolon-separated).
Indexed keywords from Scopus (e.g., MeSH or subject tags).
Narrative funding acknowledgment text included in the article.
Binary field indicating whether funding is reported (“yes” or empty).
List of references cited by the article (semicolon-separated).
Editor names; this column is empty for all records.
Name of the publishing organization (e.g., Elsevier Ltd).
Unique PubMed identifier when available; missing for non-indexed items.
Language of publication (all entries are “English”).
Type of publication (e.g., Article, Review, Editorial)
Stage of publication (e.g., Final, Pre-print)
Whether the paper is open access
Name of the database
Electronic identifier assigned by Scopus
